result:
I've saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Run with the same settings, my script reproduces all 10 of your Q2 values exactly.

The data didn't match your definitions as written in three places, so I tried variants until the Q2 numbers lined up:
- **Order dates are converted to Korean time (UTC+9).** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC. If I use UTC as-is, the Q2 results don't match (d comes out 2025-06 and h comes out +5.7). With UTC+9 they do.
- **A customer means one email address, not one customer ID.** Some emails, such as `u100@ex.com`, appear under 2–3 customer IDs. Counting by ID gives Q2 b=283 and f=232; grouping by email (trimmed, lowercased) gives the reference 235 and 193. This applies to b, e and f.
- **Segment names are cleaned up.** The data has values like `" consumer"` and `"Enterprise "`, so I trimmed spaces and lowercased them before grouping.

One more thing: there are no April orders in the DB, so Q2 effectively covers only May and June.

| Item | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment / net sales | consumer / 381,952,036 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 247 |
| c. Top category / net sales | sw / 328,381,240 |
| d. Month with highest net sales | 2025-08 |
| e. Email with the largest total refunds | u141@ex.com (1,891,815, no tie) |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 240 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 710,334 |
| h. Growth, September vs August | -30.0% |

Monthly net sales were 312,507,163 in July, 354,831,928 in August and 248,282,108 in September. September versus August is -30.03%, which rounds to -30.0.

The script is at `/work/scripts/q.py`.
